body.statement: If \(K=1\), write \(b_a=\Pr(Y_t(\infty)=a)\) and let \(h\) be the scalar hazard. Then \(P=1\), \(K_0=1-h\), \(p_g=(1-h)^gh\), \(L=h\), \(P_{\mathrm{dk}}=1\), \(\pi^0_{g,r}(z_0,\ldots,z_r)=\prod_{j=0}^r b_{z_j}\), and \(\mu^0_{g,r}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal Y}\nu(a)b_a\). If the \(K\) emission-profile vectors \(\{(B_a(s,s):a\in\mathcal Y):1\le s\le K\}\) are pairwise distinct, multivariate polynomial interpolation gives every diagonal matrix in the latent-coordinate emission algebra; hence the canonical \(L\) is similar to \(D\), \(P_{\mathrm{dk}}\) is similar to \(P\), and the observable formulas reduce exactly to \(\pi^0_{g,r}(z_0,\ldots,z_r)=\alpha K_0^gDB_{z_0}PB_{z_1}\cdots PB_{z_r}v/p_g\) and \(\mu^0_{g,r}=\alpha K_0^gDP^re/p_g\). If \(h_s=\lambda\) for every state, then \(L=\lambda I_K\) and \(P_{\mathrm{dk}}\) is similar to \(P\). For \(r=0\), \(\mu^0_{g,0}=\bar\alpha\bar K_0^gE\bar h/p_g\) without the hazard-algebra restriction.
body.justification: These reductions prevent the new formula from contradicting ordinary identified HMMs or the mechanically identified contemporaneous cohort mean.
body.gap: The reductions are sanity checks rather than novelty claims.
body.consumer: They give implementers diagnostic benchmarks for one-state, distinct-emission, constant-hazard, and contemporaneous-effect cases.
